Capabilities for ML engineers

Turn documents and custom datasets into domain-specific small language models.

BrewSLM is built for engineers fine-tuning a base model on real data. The capability families below cover the path from your documents to a verdict and a shipped model; the importer, source connectors, task mappers, task-aware evaluation and plugin contracts exist so messy domain-specific data can take the same path.

Capability families

From documents to a verdict you can trust

Documents → Q&A, with a pre-training check

One flow turns cleaned passages into training pairs plus a held-out answer key, sizes the test split for a decision, then judges the base model reading the passages before it trains. When retrieval alone is good enough, it stops.

  • Lesson 3.9: When fine-tuning isn't the answer

Auto-RAG sweep and reroute

Compares the base model, the base model with passages and the fine-tune on the same questions, sweeps the retrieval settings, and can clone a project into a retrieval-first sibling.

  • Lesson 3.9: Auto-RAG and reroute
  • The Pub 17 run where retrieval won

Paired lift, across seeds

Every finished run is scored against its own base model on the same held-out rows; the verdict reports the change with a 95% interval, says when it is within noise, and states the smallest gap the test set can detect. Check across 3 seeds repeats the run.

  • Lesson 3.8: Evaluate
  • Beyond a single run

Splits you can defend

Random splits deduplicate and stratify by default; Use my own train / val / test files imports predefined splits and refuses (or drops) training rows that leak into the test set. Data health checks training rows against the answer key.

  • Lesson 3.4: Clean and prepare

Span thresholds, recall floors, compliance bundles

Token-classification taggers get per-type decoding thresholds tuned on validation to keep recall floors, a Try redaction box, and compliance bundles (PCI DSS, GDPR, HIPAA, CCPA) that add entity types and report recall per regime.

  • Tutorial 7: PII span tagging
  • The sensitive-data tagger, built from zero

Typed JSON records

The json-extraction recipe trains text → one JSON record with fixed keys and scores it field by field: numbers compare as numbers, and a null for an unstated field is told apart from a wrong value.

  • Tutorial 3: Invoice field extraction
  • The accident-report extractor

Ship and publish

Export a run as GGUF, ONNX, TensorRT, Hugging Face or Docker; publish a Hugging Face export to the Hub; deploy versions with promote and rollback.

  • Lesson 3.10: Export, deploy and Coach

Importing existing datasets

Bring a labelled dataset: sniff columns, map, keep every row accounted for

When you already have labelled rows, the importer maps them to a task shape. Imported rows are written as accepted: they skip the review queue and train directly.

01 Schema introspector

Sniff columns, propose a mapping

Reads ~20 sample rows from any source, classifies each column by content shape (text-like, categorical, BIO tags, chat messages, etc.), ranks hypotheses with confidence + rationale. Never silently auto-picks — the user confirms via --auto above the threshold or --force under it.

You control: the threshold, the override, the field map.

02 Target mappers

Domain-agnostic, registry-driven

Each mapper declares the task profile it feeds; the tables below list the built-ins. The Kaggle PII converter that came before was 175 lines of BIO-to-spans logic; the introspector infers the same mapping from sample rows, for any BIO-tagged dataset.

You control: custom mappers via plugin modules.

03 Bulk-drop UX

Group rejects by reason, drop in one click

Per-row accountability is the contract — every raw row becomes either a TransformedRow or a RejectedRow with a stable reason code. Counts stay in the audit log even when you bulk-drop a category from the import.

You control: which rejection categories to silence.

An import session (excerpt)

$ python -m app.cli.dataset_import introspect \

    --locator hf:ai4privacy/pii-masking-200k:train

top proposal: bio_to_spans (confidence 0.95) — safe to --auto

POST /api/projects/1/dataset-import/preview

→ accepted=4982 rejected=18 (length_mismatch=18)

POST /api/projects/1/dataset-import/run

→ written_path=…/projects/1/synthetic/synthetic.jsonl

RunEvent stage=ingestion reason=dataset_import_run

What lands in your project

source: hf:ai4privacy/pii-masking-200k:train

mapper: bio_to_spans

target_task_profile: structured_extraction

scoring_mode: span_set

written_rows: 4982

saved_mapping: pii-weekly-refresh

Source connectors

Built-in connectors, plus a plugin slot

Source id Locator format What it does
jsonl jsonl:/path/to/file.jsonl One JSON object per line. Unparseable lines surface as sentinel rows.
csv csv:/path/to/file.csv First row = header. Every cell is a string; mappers handle coercion.
hf hf:<id>[:split[:revision]] Wraps datasets.load_dataset with streaming=True. Auth via HF_TOKEN for gated datasets.
kaggle kaggle:competition:<slug> Downloads + extracts via the Kaggle API. Cache under ~/.cache/brewslm/kaggle/. Multi-file disambig via ?file=….
file file:/path/to/data.{csv,tsv,jsonl,json,xlsx,parquet} Any row file; browser uploads land here. Handles encodings and delimiters. Documents (PDF, DOCX, HTML) go through Data → Upload documents instead.
git git:<url>[@ref] Shallow clone; one row per source chunk (cut at declarations) and one per prose file. Records the repo licence and pinned commit.
web web:<seed url> Polite crawl (robots.txt, prefix-limited, rate-limited, cached); one {url, title, text} row per page.
your plugin yourthing:<ref> Call register_source(id, factory) when your module is imported. Same contract as built-ins.

Target mappers

Built-in mappers, plus a plugin slot

Mapper id Task profile Use when the row carries…
bio_to_spans structured_extraction · span_set BIO-tagged tokens + labels (NER / PII)
label_to_classification classification {text, label}
text_only language_modeling a single text column, no labels
qa_pair_passthrough qa {question, answer}
chat_messages_passthrough chat_sft a messages list of {role, content} dicts
preference_pair dpo {prompt, chosen, rejected} (RLHF / DPO / ORPO)
rag_passthrough rag_qa {question, context, answer} (grounded QA)
kv_to_structured structured_extraction · field_match flat key-value extractions (invoices, forms, receipts)
code_label_to_findings structured_extraction · findings a piece of code + a label column naming what is wrong with it (or nothing)
contrast_functions structured_extraction · findings source files whose functions are named as bad / good twins
fix_pair structured_extraction · findings (or patch / preference rows) {before, after, label}: a defect and its fix
your plugin your choice Register via register_dataset_mappers(register); declare any task profile that has a registered handler.

Task-aware eval

Metrics that match the task, not the average of every task

Classification

  • Per-class precision / recall / F1 + confusion matrix.
  • Macro + micro aggregates.
  • Legacy exact_match / f1 aliases preserved for gate compat.

Span-set scoring (NER / PII)

  • Strict (type, start, end) match; off-by-one boundaries count as miss + hallucination.
  • Per-class P/R/F1 next to micro/macro.
  • Triggered by output_schema.scoring_mode: "span_set" on the manifest.

RAG

  • Answer EM/F1 + faithfulness (fraction of prediction grounded in context).
  • Context recall — tells retriever bugs from generation bugs.
  • Per-row badge next to each scored prediction.

DPO / ORPO alignment

  • Similarity-to-chosen vs similarity-to-rejected (token-level F1 proxy).
  • Mean alignment margin across rows.
  • Falls back to plain EM/F1 when chosen/rejected are absent.

Seq2Seq

  • BLEU + chrF for translation; ROUGE for summarization; both for paraphrase.
  • length_ratio reported alongside content metrics.
  • Sub-task pulled from the prepared manifest's subtask field.

Vision + audio

  • Image captioning / VQA → vision-language handler; captioning reports BLEU-4 and ROUGE-L.
  • Speech-to-text → audio-transcript handler (WER / CER).
  • Multimodal media flag enforced at preflight.

JSON records

  • Field-by-field typed match (numbers compare numerically), with token-F1 partial credit on string fields.
  • Null precision / recall: an unstated field answered null is told apart from a wrong value.
  • JSON validity and, with a declared output schema, schema compliance.

Tool calling

  • tool_selection_accuracy: the right tool was named.
  • tool_args_match_rate, and the headline tool_call_pass_rate (tool and arguments).
  • With a tool catalog, a call must also be valid against it.

Safety

  • Prompt-injection, secret-extraction, PII-regurgitation, jailbreak and unknown-answer probes.
  • Each response scored refused / complied / ambiguous by keyword heuristics.
  • Pass rate per probe type, not one coarse number.

LLM judge

  • For long free-text answers where exact match is meaningless: a judge model you configure grades each answer.
  • Reports llm_judge_pass_rate, usable as a pass/fail rule.
  • Judge calibration compares the judge with a reference model's blind labels.

Reproducibility

Save once, re-run forever, audit every time

Saved mappings

The import wizard's Save this mapping button persists (locator, mapper_id, field_map, drop_reasons) under a name. The Saved mappings panel on Data → Sources shows last-run row counts and offers one-click Re-run.

name: weekly-pii-refresh

locator: kaggle:competition:pii-detection-…

mapper_id: bio_to_spans

last_run_at: 2026-05-13T10:00:00Z

last_run_accepted: 5,012

Audit log

Every import — fresh or re-run — emits a RunEvent with stage ingestion and reason code dataset_import_run (or dataset_import_failed on errors). Payload includes the config_id link when the run came from a saved mapping.

RunEvent { stage: "ingestion",

  reason_code: "dataset_import_run",

  payload: { source_id: "kaggle",

    mapper_id: "bio_to_spans",

    accepted_count: 5012,

    rejection_counts: {length_mismatch: 18},

    config_id: 12 } }

Extensibility

Plugin contracts everywhere it matters

Source plugins

Register a new connector with register_source(id, factory); it is addressed by locator prefix. There is no settings loader for sources yet, so the call has to run at import time, for example from a module you already list under DATASET_MAPPER_PLUGIN_MODULES.

from app.services.dataset_import.registry import register_source

register_source("yourthing", YourThingSource)

Mapper plugins

Drop a module under DATASET_MAPPER_PLUGIN_MODULES; export register_dataset_mappers(register). Built-in failure isolation: one broken plugin doesn't block the rest of the load.

def register_dataset_mappers(register):

    register("my_mapper", MyMapper)

LLM-assist (opt-in)

When the deterministic sniffer can't reach 0.8 confidence, the introspector can consult your teacher model for a mapping suggestion. The LLM's proposal goes through the same confidence gate; hallucinated mapper ids are rejected.

DATASET_IMPORT_LLM_ASSIST_ENABLED=true \

python -m app.cli.dataset_import introspect --locator … --llm-assist

See the surface end-to-end

The fastest read is the source

Every capability above is one file you can read. Start with backend/app/services/dataset_import/ for the pipeline, or backend/app/services/eval_task_handler_service.py for the task handlers.

$ git clone https://github.com/TensorGreed/__SLM__ brewslm

$ cd brewslm/backend

$ ls app/services/dataset_import/

introspector.py mappers/ plugin_loader.py sources/ service.py …
